documents.title: Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity.
documents.abstract: Global soil salinization severely threatens agricultural productivity. Portulaca oleracea L., an extreme xerohalophyte, displays exceptional salinity tolerance, yet the transcriptional architecture coordinating its antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages remains unresolved. In this study, multi-tissue high-throughput RNA-Seq, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) validation, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network (GRN) modeling were integrated to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in P. oleracea. documents.title: Amino Acid Metabolic Signature Links Pediatric Environmental Enteric Dysfunction to Maternal-Fetal Growth Restriction Across Two Independent Cohorts.
documents.abstract: Environmental Enteric Dysfunction (EED) is a leading contributor to childhood stunting. Most EED literature derives from postnatal pediatric cohorts, leaving unclear how much of the metabolic signature reflects acquired intestinal pathology versus growth restriction originating earlier. We applied genome-scale metabolic modeling to explore whether metabolic features of pediatric EED overlap with those of maternal plasma proteomes associated with adverse early-life growth. documents.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
documents.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct

documents.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are ubiquitous yet elusive due to their reactivity and short half-lives, making simulation essential for mechanistic insight. documents.title: Temporal multi-omics reveals regulatory transitions and renoprotective candidates in cisplatin-induced kidney injury.
documents.abstract: Cisplatin is a classic first-line platinum drug extensively used in chemotherapy for solid tumors, yet its clinical applications are limited by dose-dependent nephrotoxicity. The dynamic molecular mechanisms underlying cisplatin-induced kidney injury and regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we established two complementary mouse models, a single high-dose cisplatin (SHDC) model and a repeated low-dose cisplatin (RLDC) model, to recapitulate acute and progressive/persistent patterns of renal injury, respectively. documents.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.
documents.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) govern many cell processes. While multistability and oscillations are common GRN dynamics, they are typically studied and engineered in isolation. Here, we challenge this separation using the AC-DC circuit, a minimal three-gene network that merges the classical toggle switch and repressilator. Using a thermodynamic formalism and Bayesian inference, we show that a single-inducer version of the circuit displays diverse multifunctional dynamics, including coexistence of oscillations and multistability. documents.title: Robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells.
documents.abstract: Cell-cell communication modulates cell fate decisions by relaying information across tissues and inducing intracellular responses mediated by gene regulatory networks. Although the inference of cell-cell communication from high-throughput data is gaining popularity, studying how communication pathways operate across biological scales and influence cell fate decisions remains challenging. Here, we present scRICH (robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells), a computational framework that leverages single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data to unravel the he

documents.title: Revisiting Ehrlich carcinoma in the era of precision oncology: bridging classical models with modern systems biology.
documents.abstract: Ehrlich carcinoma (EC) and its ascitic form, Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC), are among the oldest and most widely used experimental tumor models in cancer research. Although they have traditionally been used for anticancer drug screening, their potential to address broader aspects of aggressive tumor biology has received comparatively less attention. EC/EAC exhibits several characteristics associated with advanced malignancy, including rapid tumor growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic changes, therapeutic resistance, and complex interactions between the tumor and host. documents.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
documents.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C p

documents.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
documents.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.

documents.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
documents.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. documents.title: Metabolic modeling with reverse mapping links host perturbations to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
documents.abstract: Understanding host-pathogen interactions during Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection has largely relied on identifying bacterial genes essential for intracellular survival. However, conventional reverse genetics approaches often overlook host pathways that regulate Mtb growth. Here, we developed a backtracing strategy to link host metabolic modulators with specific Mtb proteins. A genome-scale host metabolic model integrated with lung transcriptomic data from H37Rv-infected mice predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb survival. We validated this through pharmacological inhibition, s

documents.title: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals autophagy-associated transcriptional vulnerability of dopaminergic neurons after atrazine exposure.
documents.abstract: Atrazine (ATZ) is a widely used triazine herbicide with potential neurotoxic effects, but the cell-type-specific responses of midbrain dopaminergic neurons to ATZ exposure remain poorly defined. In this study, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing to midbrain tissues from adult male mice exposed to ATZ for 28 days (a sub-acute exposure) to characterize transcriptional alterations associated with dopaminergic neuronal injury. Three mice per group were used for scRNA-seq, and group comparisons were performed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test, or the Kruskal-Wallis test with D

documents.title: Integrative analysis of Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian regulators for prioritization of drug repurposing candidates.
documents.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by complex molecular mechanisms. Growing evidence indicates that circadian rhythm disruption contributes to disease progression and interacts with pathogenic pathways. documents.title: scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.
documents.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from single-cell transcriptomes is complicated by expression patterns associated with both cell state and shared ancestry. Cellular phylogenies provide developmental context, but incorporating relationships among individual cells into gene-level regulatory inference remains challenging.

documents.title: Engineering rhizosphere microbial consortia for soil bioremediation: Mechanisms, field constraints, and evidence-based design.
documents.abstract: Soil contamination continues to threaten ecosystem health and agricultural productivity worldwide. However, rhizosphere-mediated bioremediation has emerged as a nature-inspired, sustainable approach for mitigating these impacts. This review advocates field-scale implementation of rhizosphere microbiome engineering by exploiting interactions among plants, microorganisms, and soil. Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarize rhizosphere-mediated remediation processes, it integrates mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives to identify critical barriers limiting field performance

documents.title: A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.
documents.abstract: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is the most prevalent sensory deficit in older adults, yet its molecular progression remains poorly resolved. Few cochlear single-cell studies have integrated cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction, and cross-cohort bulk validation into one temporal framework.

documents.title: Genome-scale metabolic model analysis of Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates reveals lineage-level metabolic structure.
documents.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) of Campylobacter jejuni (C. jejuni) have been studied mainly for reference strains, and their characteristics at the lineage level remain poorly understood. We reconstructed GSMMs for 86 C. jejuni isolates collected in Korea using gapseq and analyzed them together with in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. documents.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
documents.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul

documents.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
documents.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. documents.title: Decoding the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis through single-cell multiomics integration.
documents.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a prevalent chronic condition, yet the cellular and molecular changes associated with its pathogenesis remain incompletely understood.
documents.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

documents.title: Endothelial SLC25A13 links glutamine metabolism to angiogenesis.
documents.abstract: Attention to exploring endothelial cell (EC) metabolism is increasing, but a holistic perspective on the metabolic adaptations of ECs during angiogenic proliferation is still missing. Here, we use a previously in-house developed computational EC-adapted genome-scale metabolic model that recapitulates known metabolic features in proliferating ECs to predict novel pathways central to biomass synthesis. We unveil the metabolic function of the glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13, previously overlooked in ECs, as a key regulator of glutamine utilization and provide evidence regarding its contri

documents.title: A metabolic model based on a pangenome core reveals putative conserved biochemical features of the phytopathogen Xylella fastidiosa.
documents.abstract: Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited phytopathogenic bacterium responsible for severe diseases in many economically important crops. Despite its impact, its metabolism remains poorly characterized due to fastidious growth and the limited availability of defined culture media. Here, we reconstruct the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for X. fastidiosa, integrating conserved metabolic functions from 18 strains across five subspecies. The resulting consensus model, iXfcore, is manually curated and used to explore the species' metabolic capabilities. Model simulations predict mi

documents.title: Hybrid genome‑scale metabolic modeling and machine learning reveal cost‑efficient strategies for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate production in Rhodopseudomonas palustris.
documents.abstract: Plastic pollution from fossil-based materials is a major global environmental challenge. Microbially derived bioplastics, such as polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), offer a promising biodegradable alternative. However, the high substrate and operational costs of PHB production remain a major barrier to large-scale deployment. Optimizing PHB synthesis requires navigating a multidimensional design space of metabolic, nutritional, and operational variables, which is impractical to explore experimentally. This study presents an integrated computational framework that combines a genome-scale metabolic mode

documents.title: Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.
documents.abstract: This paper examines why robust causality assessment is central to toxicology yet increasingly difficult in networked biological systems, including Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks and multi-omics datasets. Classical causal frameworks (e.g., Koch/Dale reasoning and Bradford Hill-type considerations) remain useful for scoping, but they offer limited operational guidance for multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-dominated mechanisms. We therefore synthesize a modern toolbox for causality analysis in toxicology spanning directed acyclic graphs for explicit causal assumptions, quantitative

documents.title: Proteomics and network biology insights into inflammation suppression during prolonged high-altitude hypoxia acclimatization.
documents.abstract: For decades, the study of high-altitude acclimatization has been a vital area of scientific inquiry aimed at enhancing human resilience, particularly in the context of military deployments. While most existing research has focused on acute inflammatory responses to hypoxia, limited information is available on the molecular mechanisms underlying long-term high-altitude acclimatization. To address this gap, the present study investigated the plasma proteomic alterations associated with 120 days of high-altitude exposure at 14,500 ft by employing quantitative proteomics combined with computationa

documents.title: Neutrophil-microglia communication through the C3-C3aR1 axis contributes to secondary neuroinflammation after traumatic brain injury.
documents.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a rapidly evolving neuroinflammatory response that contributes to secondary brain injury. Although infiltrating leukocytes and resident microglia are both prominent components of this response, the cellular signals that connect peripheral immune-cell recruitment to microglial state remodeling remain incompletely defined.

documents.title: Bringing translational structure to complex immune-mediated conditions: the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework for divergent phenotypes.
documents.abstract: Immune-mediated outcomes diverge across individuals with similar genetic backgrounds and environmental exposures, reflecting trajectories through a dynamic, context-dependent, and partially stochastic state space rather than fixed molecular endpoints. Despite advances in systems immunology, computational modeling, and multi-omic profiling, translating this complexity into clinically actionable reasoning remains difficult: these disciplines generate increasingly detailed representations of immune behavior that deepen mechanistic understanding while raising barriers to integration across clinica

documents.title: Targeting the gut-tumor axis: probiotic therapy as an adjunct strategy in colorectal cancer treatment.
documents.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a multifactorial disease driven by interactions among host genetics, immune dysregulation, environmental factors, and gut microbiota. The gut-tumor axis regulates CRC progression through inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier disruption, and immune imbalance. Probiotic-derived metabolites act as bioactive molecules capable of restoring host-microbiome homeostasis and modulating tumor-associated pathways.
